active.name: move

team.name: yaw
team.note: The order is [yaw | a]: puts the degrees into [move | yaw | _] and sends it. Degrees are degrees -- nothing scales them.

team.name: pitch
team.note: The order is [pitch | a]: puts the degrees into [move | pitch | _] and sends it. Degrees are degrees -- nothing scales them.

team.name: roll
team.note: The order is [roll | a]: puts the degrees into [move | roll | _] and sends it. Degrees are degrees -- nothing scales them.

team.name: pendown
team.note: The word on the letterbox is “pendown”: eats it and sends [set | pen | down].

team.name: penup
team.note: The word on the letterbox is “penup”: eats it and sends [set | pen | up].

team.name: home
team.note: The word on the letterbox is “home”: eats it and sends [set | home | yes] -- level, facing the far edge, back on the table.

active.note: Leads the team. The order is [move | n]: multiplies n by the step size, puts it into [move | forward | _] and sends it -- a stride the way the turtle is pointing.

active.name: the pilot
active.note: Three orders, always the same three: [move | 10], [move | 10], [pitch | 30], each a copy given to the bird to the letterbox. Two strides then a turn, and the path closes into a loop -- no counting anywhere.

thing.text:
TAKE OFF AND LOOP

Press SPACE on THE
AIRPLANE. Two behaviours
are bound to it and both
start at once:

  a 3D turtle -- which
    gives it move, yaw,
    pitch and roll
  the pilot -- which
    speaks them

"." lands it. Its pen is
down, so it draws its own
flight path as it goes.

TRY THIS

Open the pilot's panel and
change 30 to 45: a tighter
loop. Change it to 0 and it
flies straight until the
table runs out.

Post [roll | 30] to the bird
while it loops and the loop
tilts -- roll turns about
the line of travel, so it
changes the PLANE the loop
is drawn in.

"home" puts it back on the
table, level and facing the
far edge.

IS IT A CIRCLE?

Look at the path: twelve
straight strides with a
corner after every two.
That is a twelve-sided
loop, not a circle.

Halve both: move 5, move
5, pitch 15. Rounder. Halve
again. When does it stop
looking like corners -- and
does it ever become a
circle, or only get closer?

A LOOP NEEDS NO COUNTING

The pilot's whole round is
three orders, always the
same three:

  move 10
  move 10
  pitch 30

Turn the same few degrees
every stride and the path
closes into a circle. Two
strides per turn makes the
arc wide, so it runs, lifts,
climbs, and comes over the
top. Twelve rounds is a
full 360.
